comment: Tapers on curves the draft cannot lean (mitcad#1749, GitHub #307): an ellipse and a closed spline. Their walls are ruled from the profile to its offset in the sketch plane. Sketch1 (F1): an ellipse of half-axes 20 and 10 about the origin, extruded 10 (Extrude1, F2) at +5 and at -20 degrees. The ellipse is convex and the walls move less than its least radius of curvature (5 mm), so the profile offset by d keeps the area A + P d + pi d^2 (Steiner) and the solid has h (A + P d / 2 + pi d^2 / 3), with A = 200 pi, P = 96.88448220547677 and d = 10 tan(angle). OCCT's integration of the B-spline walls is off by about 1e-3 (as for extruded splines), hence the volumes' tolerance.

Sketch2 (F3): a closed spline through four points inside the ellipse, cut through the tapered ellipse with a widening taper of 5 degrees (Extrude2, F4): the hole's wall is one face named after the spline.

Sharp corners where a spline meets lines: Sketch3 (F5), three lines and a quadratic arch by its control points (40, 120), (20, 128), (0, 120) over the top, extruded 10 (Extrude3, F6) at +5 degrees (the offsets part at the corners and run on to mitres) and at -10 degrees (they cross and end there). One wall per curve. The profile offset by d with mitred corners has the area A + P d + c d^2, with A = 2720 / 3, P = 121.04242521705052 and c = 4.534572299966166 (the tangents of the half turns at the four corners plus half the arch's turn), so the solid has 10 (A + P d / 2 + c d^2 / 3).
